activity_context.topic_title: Changing a Basis Using the Change-of-Coordinates Matrix

feedback.problem:
$$
B={[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 4\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 5\end{aligned}]},\,C={[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -3\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2\end{aligned}]},\,[x]_{C}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -5\end{aligned}]
$$

The bases $B$ and $C$ of ${R}^{2}$ and the coordinates of the vector $x$ relative to the basis $C$ are given above. Find $[x]_{B}.$
feedback.worked_solution:
Let's denote the vectors of $B$ and $C$ as ${{b}_{1},{b}_{2}}$ and ${{c}_{1},{c}_{2}}$, respectively.

The change-of-coordinates matrix from $C$ to $B$ is a matrix whose columns are the vectors of $C$ relative to the basis $B.$

Hence, we need to find the coordinates of ${c}_{1}$ and ${c}_{2}$ relative to the basis $B.$ We can do this simultaneously by considering the matrix

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}| & | & | & | \\ {b}_{1} & {b}_{2} & {c}_{1} & {c}_{2} \\ | & | & | & |\end{aligned}].
$$

Now, we simply reduce the left-hand side to reduced row-echelon form using Gaussian elimination:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 2 & 1 \\ 4 & 5 & -3 & -2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-4){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & -11 & -6\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+(-1){R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 13 & 7 \\ 0 & 1 & -11 & -6\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, the change-of-coordinates matrix ${P}_{C\to B}$ is

$$
{P}_{C\to B}=[\begin{aligned}13 & 7 \\ -11 & -6\end{aligned}].
$$

Finally, we compute $[\,x\,]_{B}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}[\,x\,]_{B} & ={P}_{C\to B}[\,x\,]_{C} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}13 & 7 \\ -11 & -6\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 \\ -5\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-9 \\ 8\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
